# 14. Common Lisp style

<!-- Generated by tools/generate-docs.lisp from docs/manual/chapters.lisp,
     docs/manual/introduction.md and the examples: do not edit by hand. -->

lib/cl.lisp gives cog-lisp the names of Common Lisp: defun, defmacro, handler-case
and their kin.

## Common Lisp style, with lib/cl.lisp loaded.

In the manner of an introductory CL text's early chapters; written for
cog-lisp.

Remember: nil is true here. Common Lisp's nil is both the empty list and
false, and cog-lisp has two values for those, () and #f; cl binds nil to (),
so that (cons 1 nil) is a proper list, and only #f is false. So (if nil ...)
takes its first branch, and so does (if (member x lst) ...) when member
answers (). Test a list with null or consp, and write #f for false.

`examples/cl-style.lisp`:

```scheme
(require 'cl)

(defun our-length (lst)
	(if (null lst) 0 (+ (our-length (cdr lst)) 1))
)

(defun our-member (obj lst)
	(cond
		((null lst) nil)
		((eql (car lst) obj) lst)
		(t (our-member obj (cdr lst)))
	)
)

(defun show-squares (start end)
	(dotimes (k (- (+ end 1) start))
		(let ((i (+ start k)))
			(display (list i (* i i)))
			(display " ")
		)
	)
	(newline)
)

(defvar *items* '(a b c d))

(display (our-length *items*))
(newline)
(display (our-member 'c *items*))
(newline)
(show-squares 2 5)

; iteration over a list, accumulating with push
(let ((acc nil))
	(dolist (x *items*)
		(push x acc)
	)
	(display acc)
	(newline)
)

; local functions with labels, and functions as values with funcall
(defun count-leaves (tree)
	(labels (
			(walk
				(x)
				(cond
					((null x) 0)
					((atom x) 1)
					(t (+ (walk (car x)) (walk (cdr x))))
				)
			)
		)
		(walk tree)
	)
)
(display (count-leaves '((a b) (c (d e)) f)))
(newline)
(display (funcall (lambda (x y) (* x y)) 6 7))
(newline)
(display (mapcar (lambda (x) (* 10 x)) '(1 2 3)))
(newline)

; a macro with defmacro and &rest
(defmacro my-unless (test &rest body)
	`(if ,test nil (progn ,@body))
)
(display (my-unless (> 1 2) 'ran))
(newline)

; setf of places: a list's elements, and a hash table used as a counter
(let ((cells (list 'a 'b 'c)) (counts (make-hash-table)))
	(setf (second cells) 'x (nth 2 cells) 'y)
	(dolist (w '(to be or not to be))
		(setf (gethash w counts) (+ 1 (gethash w counts 0)))
	)
	(display (list cells (gethash 'to counts) (gethash 'or counts)))
	(newline)
)

; the procedure keeps the text it was written as
(display (procedure-source our-length))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
4
(c d)
(2 4) (3 9) (4 16) (5 25) 
(d c b a)
6
42
(10 20 30)
ran
((a x y) 2 1)
(defun our-length (lst)
	(if (null lst) 0 (+ (our-length (cdr lst)) 1))
)
```

## The same ideas in Common Lisp style (lib/cl.lisp; Phase 7.7)

`examples/conditions-cl.lisp`:

```scheme
(require 'cl)

; handler-case: unwind, then run the clause for the condition's type.
(defun safe-divide (a b)
  (handler-case (/ a b)
    (ZeroDivide (c) 'infinity)                ; a Smalltalk exception class
    (error (c) (list 'error (error-object-message c)))))
(display (list (safe-divide 10 2) (safe-divide 1 0) (safe-divide 1 'x)))
(newline)

; ignore-errors: nil instead of an error.
(display (list (ignore-errors (car 5)) (ignore-errors (+ 1 2))))
(newline)

; unwind-protect: the cleanup runs whether or not the body fails.
(defvar *log* nil)
(defun logged (thunk)
  (ignore-errors
    (unwind-protect (funcall thunk)
      (push 'cleaned-up *log*))))
(logged (lambda () 'fine))
(logged (lambda () (error "boom")))
(display *log*)
(newline)

; handler-bind: handlers run before unwinding; this one chooses a restart.
(defun parse-number (s)
  (let ((n [s asInteger]))
    (if (smalltalk-nil? n)
        (restart-case (error "not a number:" s)
          (use-value (v) v))
        n)))
(display (handler-bind ((error (lambda (c) (invoke-restart 'use-value -1))))
           (mapcar parse-number '("1" "two" "3"))))
(newline)
```

Its output:

```text
(5 infinity (error /: not a number: x))
(() 3)
(cleaned-up cleaned-up)
(1 -1 3)
```
